note: V90Jd::packData, 0x1e960, 534 bytes.  EVERY ANCHOR HERE CARRIES packData's OWN COMMENT LINE, and that is load-bearing rather than decorative: packData's body is `getBitVector`'s body, statement for statement, because the object has the same body twice (149 instructions here against getBitVector's 150, the extra one being `lea 0x2(%edi),%eax`).  A bare statement anchor would therefore match twice and read UNUSABLE, which is exactly what happened to the `v90jd` suite's `group 0 is one bit short` when packData landed -- that row was repaired the same way, by deepening it with getBitVector's own comment rather than by a tab (findings F7521, F7580, and 432 for why a tab is the wrong repair).  The two suites are deliberately separate binaries: `v90jd` answers for the rest of the class through t_v90jd, this one answers for packData through t_v90packdata.  THE CRC'S TAP PAIR IS MUTATED HERE NOW, and it arrived from `v90jd` (finding F7944).  It used to live in a shared helper `v90jd_crc_bits`; F7940 removed that helper, because a helper taking `int *crc` and `const unsigned char *in` costs the object's promotion of the CRC register out of memory, and the three rows that anchored on the call line were re-pointed at packData's own inline copy (F7941).  `v90jd` then owned the tap claim against getBitVector's second copy of the body, and this suite deliberately had none so the claim was not scored twice.  getBitVector is now `{ packData(); return bits; }` and that copy is gone, so the row moved here rather than being lost, and `v90jd` no longer has one.  The 16/16 group question a per-group row cannot express is settled DIRECTLY instead: t_v90packdata's `run_reach` flips each of the thirty-two payload positions and requires the BLOB's CRC to move, so bits[47..50] carrying the constellation size and the lookahead are proved to reach the checksum, which is what separates this function's 16/16 from the constructor's 16/12 rate-mask split.

Writing bits[17] = 1 here cannot be observed because the very next statement in packData is `bits[V90JD_GROUP1] = 0;`, and V90JD_GROUP1 is 17: the group-0 loop runs first and the marker store overwrites it unconditionally before anything reads it.  The object has the same order -- `movb $0x1,0x2(%edi,%eax,1)` up to eax = 16 at 0x1e970, then `movb $0x0,0x13(%edi)` at 0x1e97b, where +0x13 is bits[17] -- so the two spellings differ in one store that is dead in both.  The row is kept because the ORDER is the thing that makes it dead: reverse the two statements and this mutation becomes catchable, so a future reader can see the dependency was measured rather than assumed.

why: EXPECTED UNCAUGHT, and it is an argument about the RANGE of crc[] rather than about the suite.  Every value the register can hold at this point is 0 or 1: the reset three statements earlier writes 1 into all sixteen, and the only other writes are inside the group loop's CRC block, which are either a copy of another element (crc[i] = crc[i + 1]) or the result of an expression ending in `& 1` (crc[3], crc[10] and crc[15]).  By induction over the thirty-two iterations, no element can leave {0, 1}, so masking the byte on the way out is a no-op for every reachable state -- including the states this fixture drives, where the register is SEEDED with 0x51ed0000-scale values before the call and the reset throws them away.  The object stores the whole low byte, `mov %al,0x36(%edx,%edi,1)` at 0x1eb64 with no `and` in front of it, and that is why it is written without the mask; the row records that the difference was looked for and is unobservable rather than never asked.
